purpose: Curated catalog of AOP numbered trails being assembled for park use. AOP identifies trails by NUMBER on the map (green=Easy, blue=Moderate, black=Difficult); names here are observation-confirmed by the park team and also appear in onX. This is a working/authoring seed — it will be refined and is not final form. Not yet wired to map geometry (real per-trail centerlines are still owed; see brain/tasks/01_mvp/_done/community_trails_import.md). Sources retained per row so provenance stays intact.
provenance_note: Descriptions are original AOP wording, written in the project's own voice (brain/voice/voice_guide.md). The facts behind them — difficulty, obstacles, terrain, what each trail connects to — were cross-checked against onX trail guides and in-park observation; the wording is not onX's. Trail 96 keeps the park's own 2015 blog description (via Wayback). Names confirmed against in-park observation by the park team (2026-05-29).

trails.name: Launchpad
trails.description: Packed dirt and a gentle climb to open. At Area 51 the tread breaks into loose rock and the ride turns choppy — still an easy line, just no longer smooth.

trails.name: Convergence
trails.description: An easy spur off Launchpad, bending toward the buggy side of the park. Mountain runoff gathers here and drains into Battle Creek — that's the convergence it's named for.

trails.name: Major Tom
trails.description: Reads casual, and that's the catch. Accessible enough to wave through, but a starter rig or anything low on clearance can get caught out the moment attention drops.

trails.name: Lifeform
trails.description: A quiet uphill connector. Small rock, exposed roots, a few bends, and it feeds you back out onto Trail 3.

trails.name: Descension
trails.description: A mild descent that opens on a dirt flat and saves the work for the bottom: a deep, eroded rut with a tree root sitting square in the line.

trails.name: Ascension
trails.description: A hill climb that lives and dies on traction. Dry, it's a good time for any rig. Wet, it goes greasy in a hurry.

trails.name: Little Dipper
trails.description: A full loop back to its own start, with feeders branching off to harder trails. Flat and clean nearly the whole way, with next to nothing in the way of obstacles.

trails.name: Ground Control
trails.description: Up a bit, down a bit, over and over — a short, rolling run. Rock turns up in clusters, but none of it is hard to clear.
A short loop with many rock and ledge obstacles that challenge drivers to negotiate angles and clearance. Passable by modified Jeeps and Trucks.
trails.note: Park's own 2015 description; the park referred to it by number only. Kept as the park's own wording.

coverage.estimated_total_trails: 120+ (park claim); map shows numbers into the 90s
coverage.backbone_note: The remaining ~110 numbered trails carry only a number + difficulty color on the map. They get added to this catalog as field observation, onX, or park-supplied names land. No fabricated entries.
coverage.map_marker_layer: website/data/sfwda_traced_markers.geojson — 124 georeferenced markers from the SFWDA 2015 paper map; 117 carry a hand-read trail_number (72 distinct; 116/117 in difficulty band). Contiguous per-trail geometry in website/data/sfwda_numbered_trails.geojson (67 trails). A trail's number is labelled at several points along its route. Built by mvp/scripts/run_paper_trace_pipeline.sh.

difficulty_bands_on_map.note: Approximate banding; not a hard rule.

coverage.difficulty_source_note: Two rating systems can disagree. The PARK MAP color is the park's own rating (authority for park use); onX technical ratings are onX's. Known mismatch: trails 6 (Descension) and 7 (Ascension) read GREEN/Easy on the park map but onX rates them Moderate (TR6/TR5). The 'difficulty' values above currently follow onX; reconcile to the map color during curation.
